questions.stem: Farhan has to enter the unit in which force is measured in his science record. Give that unit in full, as it is written, and give its symbol.

markingPoints.description: The SI unit of force is the newton

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The newton; its symbol is N.

evidence:
The SI unit of force is the newton (written with a small ‘n’) and its symbol
is N.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: An object is held completely inside a liquid. In which direction does the liquid push on the object, and what is this force called?

markingPoints.description: The liquid pushes on the object in the upward direction
This force is called the buoyant force

answerScheme.modelAnswer: In the upward direction; it is the buoyant force.

evidence:
itself due to the gravitational force; buoyant force exerted by liquid in an

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A toy car is pushed across a floor. State what happens to the effect of the push if only its magnitude is changed, and what happens if only its direction is changed.

markingPoints.description: Changing only the magnitude of the force also changes its effect
Changing only the direction of the force also changes its effect

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The effect of the force also changes in both cases.

evidence:
If either the magnitude or direction, or the both, of a force applied on an
object changes, the effect of the force also changes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.topic: The Force of Friction: Often Overlooked but Always Present
questions.stem: A stationary block of mass 25 kg rests on a horizontal floor where the maximum force of friction opposing the motion is 50 N. A student pushes it with a constant force of 50 N in the forward direction. State what happens to the block, and give the net force acting on it.

markingPoints.description: The net force acting on the block is zero

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The block remains stationary; the net force acting on it is zero.

evidence:
The force applied by the student is equal to the opposing force of
friction. Thus, the two forces are balanced and the net force acting on
the block is zero. So, the block will remain stationary.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
At a science exhibition, Ishan sets out a bar magnet and a wooden block. He first pushes the block along the floor and feels the block push back against his hand. He then holds the north pole of his magnet close to the north pole of a second magnet, and afterwards close to its south pole. A visitor asks him to write down the direction of each force he has felt, so that his display card can be read by everyone who comes to his stall.

State the direction in which the force of friction acts on the block as Ishan pushes it along the floor. (ii) State what happens when the north pole of Ishan's magnet is brought close to the north pole of the second magnet, and what happens when it is brought close to the south pole. (iii) Ishan says all three trials show the same force, since in each case something pushes or pulls. Using the direction of the force in each trial, explain why his claim is wrong.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) Opposite to the direction of the motion of the block. (ii) Like poles repel each other and unlike poles attract each other. (iii) The direction of the force differs in the three trials, so they cannot be one and the same force.

evidence:
an object in a direction opposite to the direction of its motion; like poles of
a magnet repelling each other or unlike poles attracting each other due to

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
Meera is in the school kitchen. She squeezes a lemon hard between her fingers, and the lemon gives way and changes shape. On the sports field that same afternoon, a batter swings the bat and the ball leaves his hands travelling in a new direction. Meera says both things show the same kind of force at work, because in each case a push from outside has changed what an object is doing. Her friend Anil disagrees and asks her to say exactly what changes in each case.

State what the force applied by Meera's fingers does to the lemon. (ii) State what the force applied by the cricket bat does to the ball's motion. (iii) Meera says the two cases show the same change because a force was applied in both. Using what the force does in each case, explain why her claim is wrong.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) It squeezes the lemon, so the shape of the lemon changes. (ii) It changes the direction of the ball's motion. (iii) The two forces have different effects, one changing the shape of the lemon and the other changing the direction of the ball's motion, so the same change did not occur in both cases.

evidence: you apply a force, a force applied by a cricket bat on a cricket ball
changes its direction, and a lemon can be squeezed by the force

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
On the school ground, a teacher hands Kavya a hammer and asks her to record what she finds. She notes that the Earth pulls the hammer down towards itself, and that a rubber ball dropped beside it also comes down. She then measures how hard she has to push a large wooden crate across the floor, and she tries the same push once more with the crate's handle tilted to one side. Her friend Ravi asks her what would happen to the push if she changed only the direction in which she pushed, but kept the strength of the push the same.

State the force with which the Earth pulls the hammer down, and the direction in which that force acts. (ii) Ravi asks what happens to the effect of Kavya's push if she changes only the direction of the push and keeps the magnitude the same. State the answer. (iii) Kavya writes down only the magnitude of each force she measured, leaving out the direction. Using the way a force has to be described, explain why her record is incomplete.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) It is the gravitational force, acting downwards, towards the Earth. (ii) The effect of the force also changes. (iii) A force is a physical quantity for which direction must be specified along with its magnitude and unit, so a record giving only the magnitude is incomplete.

questions.subject: Science
questions.topic: The Force of Friction: Often Overlooked but Always Present
questions.stem:
In a cricket match, a fielder takes a fast-moving ball close to his hands and then, just after catching it, slowly pulls his hands backwards along the direction in which the ball was travelling. In a car, a passenger wears a seat belt, and an airbag inflates quickly into a soft cushion when the car stops suddenly after a collision. A student watching both asks why the car maker thought an airbag was needed at all, when the seat belt was already being worn.

State what the airbag does when a vehicle stops abruptly after a collision, and how this reduces the force exerted on the passenger. (ii) The student says the seat belt alone is enough and the airbag is unnecessary. Using what the airbag does to the time over which the passenger is stopped, explain why the student is wrong.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (i) It inflates quickly into a soft compressible cushion, so the head and chest push into the bag instead of the hard steering wheel or dashboard; the time of the hit increases, and smaller acceleration means a reduced force on the person. (ii) The bag increases the time over which the passenger is stopped, so the acceleration is smaller and the force on the person is reduced.

evidence:
the airbag inflates quickly into
a soft compressible cushion.

head and chest push into the bag, and the time over
which the hitting occurs increases. Smaller acceleration

means a reduced force exerted on the person, thereby
lowering the risk of serious injuries
